Whole source, native pointer partial 1-3s, then equal-handle temporal point 1s. Main player stays at 0.12s. Each time change produces a new capture version; audio retains no video-frame asset.

interactions: One-use selection preview; trusted pointer and Tab confirmation; program focus and synthetic Tab stay previews.
Escape consumes preview; removing a confirmed reference retains that consumed state; reference-only direct Send works.
Object and current-session task search keeps cross-kind order and distinct object IDs for one shared asset.
Blank points, contained object positions, cross-boundary regions and mixed media use their correct coordinate spaces.
Actual DOM painted owner wins; letterbox points and content-crossing regions stay in world space; explicit target changes remain available.
Text edits reuse the image; target changes, delayed saves and cancelled native screenshots preserve the current version and owner.
Lost PNG reload, reopen and Done preserve unavailable state; explicit Capture again completes a new version.
Sampling hides fixed controls for corner and full-viewport images; restore exposes pointer cancellation while saving remains active; Escape cancels sampling.
History reads its captured scene and offers current target location separately; sent markers leave the default canvas.
Ordinary pages retain incomplete comments and open the managed capture window for Retry.
320px light and dark layouts, native keyboard events, CDP touch events and reduced motion pass.
Browser composition and keyCode 229 events protect IME confirmation; targeted existing text/file paste coverage passes.
limits: Native operating-system IME configuration was preserved; automated IME checks use browser composition events.
The local task queue and readable requirement text are delivered; automatic messaging to a host conversation remains a separate integration.
Earlier Chromium startup timeouts remain recorded as intermediate failures. Successful startups also logged display-link warnings; their causal relationship is unproven.

Temporal point uses timeStart with timeEnd omitted. The scene PNG records visible media and spatial mark; editor PNGs separately show the chosen time controls. Representative frame generation requests the chosen start time; no exact presented-frame timestamp is claimed.
